The engine socket silently hard-caps every search at ~30s wall time (go movetime N with N>30000, and go infinite, both return bestmove at 30.0s) and appears to spawn a fresh process / clear hash on each 'go', so consecutive searches don't accumulate. Not documented anywhere.
The engine socket only exposes Threads (max 2) and Hash options; MultiPV setoption is silently ignored (no error), which was confusing.
CPU appears throttled to roughly 70-100k nps total across all connections, so parallel connections don't help. Fine as a design choice, just undocumented.

The scoring (win=1, draw=0, loss=0) combined with a full-strength Stockfish opponent that replies in ~6s makes the task essentially unwinnable by design; it also creates a perverse incentive to avoid drawn repetitions at any cost (which is exactly what lost me the game). If you want to measure chess skill, a weaker opponent or partial credit for draws would give a much better signal.
